key_insight: The paper proposes a self-evolving, expert-in-the-loop annotation framework that uses LLMs plus human verification to create DSM-5-TR-aligned, explainable depression labels.
clinical_relevance: It aims to improve the transparency, auditability, and consistency of Major Depressive Disorder datasets used for mental health research, not to make clinical diagnoses.
method: Selects candidate evidence from text records
Maps evidence to DSM-5-TR criteria at the symptom level
Synthesizes case-level labels using Example Memory and Reflection Memory to incorporate expert feedback without retraining
evidence_signal: A pilot study with expert-reviewed samples reported improved annotation consistency and explainability with less manual revision effort.
watch_item: The framework’s impact across repeated feedback cycles is still untested, so real-world robustness and scalability remain to be shown.
paper_title: Self-Evolving Human-Centered Framework for Explainable Depression Symptom Annotation
